title: Buddies, candies and fixes
notes: Family Candy: every evolution family has its own Candy now, a wrapped sweet in that family’s colours, Pokémon GO style. You’ll see it in the Lab, on power-ups and when your Buddy finds some (thanks biomega9!).

Compare before you swap: with a full party, a Pokémon’s card has Swap in… Pick who makes room and see both side by side: every stat as it fights, the total and IVs, with the difference on each line (thanks jordanh_!).

Poké Ball auto-sell: Catch rules → Auto-sell spare balls. Pick how many of each ball to keep; balls you find above that sell at once for the Mart’s buy-back price. What you buy at the Mart always stays, and it never sells below your auto-buy number (thanks funloock!).
See how many trainers are online right now (Friends tab).
Classic layout: when the banner has room, your whole team walks behind your trainer, Buddy first (thanks funloock!).

Re-trading: a Pokémon you got in a trade can be traded again 14 days after it arrived (it used to be once ever). Trade levels, the daily limit and the fee still apply. Its card says when it can go again (thanks steevenss!).
changes: Buddy hearts are per Pokémon now, like Pokémon GO: each Pokémon earns up to 6 hearts a day. You can swap Buddy 3 times a day (going back to one you had today is free); the pips on Change show what’s left (thanks para82!).

Gift pop-ups: never more than one at a time (“3 gifts waiting”), none once you’ve opened today’s gifts (the Inbox says when they open again), Later means no gift pop-ups until tomorrow, and a gift never pops up twice.
Holding an item: the PC and party filter (Show → Holding an item, now near the top) and the search words item / holding also find Pokémon holding a Mega Stone or orb (thanks para82!).
The same message never stacks on screen: it shows once.

What you missed only shows after you were really away: your whole PC idle for 15 minutes (or the screen locked), not while you were busy on another monitor. Once per time away (thanks to everyone who reported it!).
fixes: Pokémon past their evolution level now evolve on their own everywhere: when caught, out of the Day Care and in the PC (Shiny, Umbral, Prismana and Perfect ones still wait for you) (thanks sgblaziken and .__.kiki.__.!).
The money on the top bar drops the moment you buy something (it used to wait for the fight on screen to finish).
Wonder Trade: the Wonder Trade it! button is always on screen now, even in a small window (the card shrinks to fit) (thanks hypergon1370!).
Professor’s Lab: the Pokémon no longer shake across the screen at some window sizes (thanks iwrecked22!).
Slots: the bet you picked is clearly lit now (thanks sato0007!).
Modular layout: an opened panel sits over the Poké Ball menu again, and the menu tucks in when a panel opens.
Always on top off: when the game is behind other windows, one click on the tray icon brings it straight back (it used to hide it first) (thanks lordyamoshi!).
Login with Discord: the rest of your screen stays clickable while the browser login is open, and the game steps back so the browser can come to the front (thanks _saltbae_!).
Founders who had the game open during the launch reset see their Founder pick without restarting.
An account that started fresh after the launch reset could stay locked out of gifts and trades: it unlocks by itself now.

Testers: linking Discord never quietly starts a new account any more. If your old guest login is gone from this PC, the login card says so before anything happens and shows your old account’s id, so the team can move your Founder reward and friends.

title: Welcome to the full launch!
notes: Welcome to the full launch! Tallgrass is open to everyone in the Glowbugs Discord now. Log in with Discord (testers: link Discord to the account you already play on, so you keep your friends, friend code and Founder reward).
Every trainer starts a fresh adventure today: your name, friend code and friends stay, and your old save is kept in your save folder as save-pre-launch.json.

Every tester is a Founder: a Founder badge next to your name everywhere (friends, leaderboards, raid parties, trades), and a thank-you gift: pick any of the 27 starters as a Prismana with perfect IVs, the Founder Ribbon and your Founder number. Founder Pokémon stay with their trainer forever. Thank you for testing!

Also new since 0.51 (details below): raid parties with friends, the Discord login, Send all / Claim all gifts, PC Rarest first + Keep sorted, Catch list types and rarities, your own Master Ball rules, multi-turn moves, What you missed, the Ready to evolve filter, and lots of fixes.
changes: A longer adventure: every island now has more bosses to beat before its Gym (6, 20, 50, 100, 140, 170, 200 and 220) and Pokémon level up a little slower, so each island gets its time to shine. The first islands are still quick; the full journey to the 8th badge is now about a week and a half of play.

Trade levels: trading grows with your friendship. New friends trade Common and Uncommon Pokémon (Trade Lv1). Lv2 adds Rare ones after 3 days as friends and 3 gifts opened between you; Lv3 adds Shiny, Alpha and Perfect after 7 days and 10 gifts; Lv4 adds Legendary, Mythical, Umbral and Prismana after 14 days and 20 gifts. Gifts both ways count. The hearts next to a friend’s name show your level: point at them to see what unlocks next.

Trading: 5 trades a day each (live trades and accepted offers), and you can receive a Pokémon once you’ve reached the island it lives on. Every trade has a small fee for the Pokémon you get, by rarity: $1,000, $10,000, $50,000 or $250,000. Locked Pokémon show a heart padlock with the level they need.
Wonder Trade and the Night Market bring you Pokémon from islands you’ve reached; Legendary, Mythical, Umbral and Prismana ones from your 5th badge.

Master Balls are rarer, so each one feels special: fewer from achievements and the Stamp book, wild Legendaries drop them less often, a Prismana sent to the Professor now gives a Big Nugget, and raids give at most one a day (still for a 50,000 hit).
Raids: everyone who helps still gets their Raid Eggs. The defeat bonus ($5,000, 2 Rare Candy, Candy and tickets) comes with 2,000 or more damage that counted.

Money and Rare Candy: Amulet Coin goes up to level 10, power-ups cost twice as much money (a good use for late-game savings), Legendaries pay less at the Professor, and Rare Candy drops a bit less often (every 30 Pokémon sent to the Professor = a Rare Candy).

title: What you missed
notes: What you missed: come back after 5 minutes or more without touching the game and a card shows everything special your team did meanwhile: Shiny, Umbral, Prismana, Alpha and Legendary catches, eggs the Nanny hatched, raid results, bosses, drops and badges. One click on Got it and you’re back (thanks terodon!).

Ready to evolve: a new filter in the PC and the party picker (Show → Ready to evolve), and the search word “ready”. It finds everything that can evolve right now: at its level, waiting for your pick, or with its stone in your Bag. Party cards get the green evolve arrow too (thanks para82!).
changes: Your catch rules always win now: anything a rule always catches (your Catch list, Legendaries, new species, Shiny and other looks, perfect IVs) is never knocked out. Your team leaves it at 1 HP and throws instead; if the balls run out, it gets away rather than fainting. Catch everything still lets your team finish the rest (thanks sato0007 and foxelina!).

A new badge no longer stops the hunt: the badge screen carries on by itself after 20 seconds (5 if you’re away). Pick Fly there or Stay right on it and the game remembers it for the next island. Point at the card to hold it (thanks dumpling4516 and sato0007!).

Start a new game is much harder to press by accident: it lists exactly what you’d lose (Pokémon, Pokédex, items, money, badges), then you type RESET or hold the red button for 3 seconds. Esc or a click outside cancels (thanks kxrciixd!).
Silvally is Legendary now, like Type: Null. The Mega, Primal, Origin and fusion forms of Legendaries count as Legendary too (thanks donpe!).
fixes: Bosses on the strip no longer poke out over the top or slide under the bar above it: big bosses and big Legendaries are sized to fit inside the strip (thanks iwrecked22!).
Tower: the end of a run now opens over the Tower page, with your recruits on pages that fit and the Claim button always in view, so you can always pick the one to take home (thanks erkumo!).
PC: long names no longer push the nickname button, gender and favourite star off the card on smaller screens. The name shortens with “…” and shows in full when you point at it (thanks erkumo!).
Eggs: the egg call and the badge on the menu go away the moment you hatch, instead of staying until the battle on the strip finished (thanks sato0007!).
